newsitem.title: INDIA: India to deregulate sugar exports - newspapers.
newsitem.headline: India to deregulate sugar exports - newspapers.

text.p: Indian newspapers said on Friday that Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet has decided to deregulate sugar exports by ending a trading agency's monopoly over foreign sales.
Business Line and Business Standard newspapers said the cabinet took the decision this week to end the Indian Sugar and General Industries Export Import Corp's (ISIGEC) monopoly.
A formal announcement of the decision was put off, however, to allow the government to gauge its political implications, Business Standard said.
Government officials could not be reached for comment.
ISIGEC is a private company set up by the sugar milling industry. Currently all exports are funnelled, or "canalised", through ISIGEC.
Currently the Sugar Export Promotion Act (SEPA) of 1958 stipulates that the country can export up to 20 percent of total sugar production, Business Line said.

On Monday, Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah told parliament the government had authorised the Food Ministry to permit the export of 1.0 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 (October-September) season.
It was not clear whether SEPA would be amended to allow more than 20 percent of total production to be exported.
